label: October 2026

biggest.lede: We move the clock back by one second as worsening Ebola outbreak and severe Australian storms increase immediate biological and climate risks.

title: Ebola Outbreak Pushes Clock Back
summary: The clock started October at 85 seconds and ended at 84 seconds, moving closer to midnight. The single biggest factor was the worsening Ebola outbreak in Central Africa, which raised biological and climate risk assessments.

sections.heading: What moved the clock
body: The Doomsday Clock was set back by one second on October 31, moving from 85 to 84 seconds, indicating a closer approach to midnight. Experts cited a worsening Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo, with deaths exceeding 5,000 and suspected cases in Nigeria, as a key driver of increased biological risk. Severe storms in Australia also heightened climate risk, reinforcing the decision to move the clock backward.

sections.heading: Where the experts disagreed
body: No experts disagreed this month; all votes were either hold or worse, with no day showing both a "worse" and a "better" vote.

sections.heading: What to watch next month
body: Monitor the spread of Ebola in Central Africa and the response efforts, as further escalation could prompt additional clock adjustments. Watch for developments in Australian weather patterns and any emerging climate-related disasters that could influence future risk assessments.
